summary: Confirmed DONE, fixed by #710 (60633eff3; also in the Hub's vendored 7bc39eec3). The server now has one favicon resolver per server (server.ts:552). It keeps an in-memory cache with a 10 min TTL that also caches absent icons, dedupes in-flight reads, and batches up to 16 roots per isolated child with 2 children at once. It has per-child deadlines and a 30 s caller deadline in place of the old 5 s timeout that counted queue time. The client cache is keyed by environment + project + avatar revision, not by connection, and every ProjectFavicon (sidebar, palette, switcher, inbox) waits until it is near the viewport. The old per-connection, per-project spawn cost is gone. What is left is small: (1) a stalled or unfinished read still reaches clients as plain null, which the client caches as 'no icon' for 5 min; (2) when a child writes nothing, the first root of its batch is blamed and backs off; (3) the optional proposal parts (persisted fingerprint cache, iconRevision, ETag GET) were not built, so a new tab still sends cheap readIcon RPCs that hit the server cache.

evidence.note: RESOLVED_ICON_TTL_MS 10 min, STALLED_ROOT_BACKOFF_MS 60 s, ICON_CACHE_CAPACITY 1024, READER_CHILDREN 2, ROOTS_PER_CHILD 16, READ_ICON_DEADLINE 30 s (lines 11-20). At f1be4abc7 this was Semaphore(2) + Effect.timeout('5 seconds') around permit + child, with no cache.

readIcon: cache hit, else join the pending deferred, else queue. Found and absent icons are remembered (line 80). Unavailable roots are not; the first one gets a 60 s backoff (line 87) and the rest get one retry child (89-93).
ProjectFaviconResolverLive is provided once at runtime level, so the cache and batching are shared across connections and tabs (ws/context.ts:292 only looks the service up).

readProjectFavicons spawns one process.execPath --eval child for many roots. Its deadline is 1.5 s + 250 ms per extra root (105-108), and roots it finished survive a kill (114-125). The worker (projectFaviconWorker.ts:98-112) writes one JSON line per root, which keeps the cloud-file isolation.

entryKey = project + avatar revision inside a per-environment LRU (64 entries / 8 MiB). There is no connectedAt or generation, so reconnects and remounts reuse icons for PROJECT_ICON_TTL_MS = 5 min. Rejected reads are not cached.

Residual: a null result is cached for 5 min like a real 'no icon'. The server cannot say 'unavailable' because ProjectReadIconResult is Schema.NullOr(...) (packages/contracts/src/project.ts:204) and readProjectIcon.ts:32-33 turns every resolver null into null.

Every web ProjectFavicon waits until it is near the viewport (useHasIntersectedViewport, effect at 93-107 needs `visible`). The sidebar also defers by header (SidebarProjectHeader.tsx:85, 129). Proposal part 4 is done for all web callers.

Tests cover shared children (<=2 batches for 20 roots, none on re-read), no negative caching of unfinished reads with a 60 s backoff (116-148), and recovery from a broken batch (152-182). The broken-batch test also shows root '/a' gets null and backs off after a spawn failure.
The legacy GET /api/project-favicon uses the same cached resolver. It still sends no ETag or validators (proposal part 3 not done) and accepts any cwd, which is pre-existing behaviour behind auth.

remaining: Nothing that keeps the original cost (per-connection, per-project spawns with no server cache) alive. Optional leftovers: (a) the server cache is memory-only with a fixed 10 min TTL and no stat fingerprint (ProjectFaviconResolver.ts:11, 80). After a restart or TTL expiry the next near-viewport request spawns ceil(P/16) children again, and a newly added or changed repo icon can be stale for up to 10 + 5 min. (b) There is no iconRevision on the project shell, so a new tab, or a remount after the 5 min client TTL, still sends readIcon RPCs for near-viewport rows. These hit the server cache, but over a Hub relay found icons are resent as base64 (up to about 683 KiB). (c) GET /api/project-favicon (http.ts:733-765) has no ETag or immutable caching.
fixDefects: Minor, no regression versus f1be4abc7: (1) An unfinished read (stall, child deadline, spawn failure, 30 s caller deadline) is settled as null (ProjectFaviconResolver.ts:70, 88, 92, 128) and goes over the wire as null. The client cannot tell it from 'no icon', caches it for 5 min (projectIconSource.ts:97-104), and a mounted row never refetches until it remounts or reconnects (ProjectFavicon.tsx:93-107). So 'timed-out results must not be negative-cached as no icon' only holds on the server; these cases are now rare. (2) Blame for a stall goes to 'the first unfinished root' (ProjectFaviconResolver.ts:84-88). When a child writes nothing at all (slow Electron start under boot load, spawn error), root 0 is backed off for 60 s and shows the fallback even though it did not stall. (3) Cache memory is bounded by entries, not bytes (1024 x up to 512 KiB in theory). The legacy HTTP route takes any cwd, so an authenticated caller could fill it. This is low risk.
implementationSketch: Only worth doing as cleanup. (1) Unavailable vs absent: make ProjectFaviconResolverShape.readIcon return a three-way result (found / absent / unavailable), or fail with a tagged ProjectIconUnavailable on unavailable, stalled-backoff and deadline paths in ProjectFaviconResolver.ts. In readProjectIcon.ts map unavailable to the existing ProjectReadIconError so the RPC rejects; projectIconSource already skips caching rejections. In http.ts, serve the fallback SVG with Cache-Control: no-store for unavailable. Optionally have web and mobile ProjectFavicon retry once after about 60 s on rejection. Tests: extend ProjectFaviconResolver.test.ts so a stalled root yields 'unavailable' rather than null; add a projectRpc test that the RPC errors; projectIconSource.test.ts already covers 'retries failed reads'. (2) Stall attribution: have readProjectFavicons report how many lines the child wrote (or whether it exited from the deadline vs a spawn error). In readBatch, when zero lines arrived, retry the whole batch once without backing off root 0. Add a resolver test for 'child emits nothing, then succeeds'. (3) Optional: add a byte budget to the server cache (reuse @ryco/shared/lruCache with a byte cap), and/or the proposal's iconRevision (hash of found bytes, or 'none') on OrchestrationProjectShell so clients can skip readIcon, plus an ETag on /api/project-favicon. The iconRevision part touches contracts and the projection, so it is M effort for little gain.
decisionReason: The residual fixes stay inside the server resolver, readProjectIcon and the client icon cache, using the existing ProjectReadIconError contract. They involve no auth, E2EE, hosted lifecycle or Hub protocol change. Only the optional iconRevision on the project shell would change a shared contract, and it is not recommended now.
